evidence_refs.title: Sample summary: when invasive treatment is discussed in coronary artery disease
Sample summary: medicines as part of care for stable coronary disease

name: Cardiology

findings.statement: High-sensitivity troponin was raised at 182 ng/L (reference below 34).
The February ECG showed ST-segment changes in the lateral leads.
The angiography report describes about 80 % narrowing in the LAD artery.
These findings together are the type of picture in which angioplasty is commonly discussed.
For stable symptoms, medicines-first approaches are also sometimes discussed as an alternative.

uncertainties.text: Whether treatment should happen within weeks or be planned later is not settled by the documents.
uncertainties.resolvable_by: Discussion with the treating cardiologist, plus an echocardiogram

missing_info.why_it_matters: Heart pumping strength may influence timing and approach.
Can help show how much the narrowing limits blood flow.

considerations.statement: A discussion of alternatives, including medicines first, may help the person understand why one path was preferred.

limitations: Angiography images were not available, only the written report.

questions.text: Is taking antiplatelet medicines together with diclofenac safe for me around the procedure?

evidence_refs.title: Sample summary: antiplatelet medicines and NSAIDs

confidence.reason: The medicine list is clear and legible.

findings.statement: Two antiplatelet medicines (aspirin and clopidogrel) are listed.
Diclofenac (an NSAID painkiller) is listed alongside antiplatelet medicines. This combination is associated with a higher chance of bleeding and is worth reviewing with the prescriber.
